```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
# Bash chunks are a record of commands you ran in the Terminal. Knitting shows
# them but doesn't run them again.
knitr::opts_hooks$set(engine = function(options) {
  if (options$engine == "bash") options$eval <- FALSE
  options
})
```

Notes for [Workshop 2](https://mb5370.bioinformatics.guide/workshop2.html). Run the commands for this workshop in the Terminal, from inside the folder named under each heading. Copy each command you run into a bash chunk.

## Redbean assembly

Commands run in `redbean/`.

Running redbean in the redbean folder:

```{bash}
cd ~/mb5370-workshops/redbean
```

Collect a small subset of data for the initial assembly.

```{bash}
cat /pvol/data/amtp4/*_[012].fastq > amtp4.fastq
```

Run the assembly (took around \~40 seconds.)

```{bash}
wtdbg2 -x ont -g 5m -t 4 -i amtp4.fastq -fo amtp4
wtpoa-cns -t 4 -i amtp4.ctg.lay.gz -fo amtp4.ctg.fa
```

Inspect assembly statistics

```{bash}
assembly-stats amtp4.ctg.fa
```

The assembly is somewhat contiguous, but likely not nearly complete.

**Table 1:** Assembly statistics output

| STATISTIC | RESULT | MEANING |
|----------------------------|-----------------------|---------------------|
| Total assembly length | 3,816,933 bp | All contigs together contain \~3.82 Mb of sequence |
| Number of contigs | 129 | The assembly is split into 129 separate pieces |
| Average contig length | 29,589 bp | Mean contig size is \~29.6 kb |
| Largest contig | 159,611 bp | The longest continuous assembled sequence is \~160 kb |
| N50 | 48,075 bp | 50% of the assembly is contained in contigs ≥48,075 bp |
| N90 | 13,023 bp | 90% is contained in contigs ≥13,023 bp |
| Ns | 0 | No ambiguous `N` bases |
| Gaps | 0 | No gaps represented in the assembly |
| Total assembly length | 3,816,933 bp | All contigs together contain \~3.82 Mb of sequence |

Run redbean with higher coverage: redo the assembly using a better coverage depth (\~20x coverage). This took around \~153.263 sec.

```{bash}
cat /pvol/data/amtp4/*.fastq > amtp4_20x.fastq
wtdbg2 -x ont -g 5m -t 4 -i amtp4_20x.fastq -fo amtp4_20x
wtpoa-cns -t 4 -i amtp4_20x.ctg.lay.gz -fo amtp4_20x.ctg.fa
```

Inspect assembly statistics

```{bash}
assembly-stats amtp4_20x.ctg.fa
```

**Table 2**: Output from assembly statistics

| STATISTIC | RESULT | MEANING |
|------------------------|----------------|---------------------------------|
| Total assembly length | 7,072,581 bp | All contigs together contain \~7.07 Mb of sequence |
| Number of contigs | 92 | The assembly is split into 92 separate pieces |
| Average contig length | 76,876 bp | Mean contig size is \~76.9 kb |
| Largest contig | 3,344,015 bp | The longest continuous assembled sequence is \~3.34 Mb |
| N50 | 1,764,942 bp | 50% of the assembly is contained in contigs ≥1,764,942 bp |
| N90 | 27,112 bp | 90% of the assembly is contained in contigs ≥27,112 bp |
| Ns | 0 | No ambiguous `N` bases |
| Gaps | 0 | No gaps represented in the assembly |
| Total assembly length | 7,072,581 bp | All contigs together contain \~7.07 Mb of sequence |

This assembly is more contiguous, there are less gaps too.

## Flye assembly

Commands run in `flye_genome/`.

Redirected to the correct folder: `cd ~/mb5370-workshops/flye_genome`

Run flye on both datasets

```{bash}
ln -s ../redbean/amtp4.fastq .
ln -s ../redbean/amtp4_20x.fastq .
```

Created .sh file to run flye_genome. Pasted in:

`#!/bin/bash #SBATCH --time=60 #SBATCH --ntasks=4 --mem=10gb`

`echo "Starting flye in $(pwd) at $(date)"`

`flye --nano-raw amtp4.fastq --out-dir amtp4 --genome-size 5m --threads 4`

`echo "Finished flye in $(pwd) at $(date)"`

... and the n ran `sbatch run_flye_small.sh` in the terminal.

Check my job status:

```{bash}
squeue
```

I can look at my job file in the directory:

```{bash}
tail slurm-300.out
```

This shows the output from the flye command as it is running.

Use the `assembly-stats` program to assess the contiguity and completeness of this assembly.

```{bash}
assembly-stats amtp4/assembly.fasta
```

Table 3: Assembly outputs from the small flye dataset

| STATISTIC | RESULT | MEANING |
|-------------------------------|----------------------|-------------------|
| Total assembly length | 5,185,224 bp | All contigs together contain \~5.19 Mb of sequence |
| Number of contigs | 77 | The assembly is split into 77 separate pieces |
| Average contig length | 67,341 bp | Mean contig size is \~67.3 kb |
| Largest contig | 368,928 bp | The longest continuous assembled sequence is \~369 kb |
| N50 | 119,681 bp | 50% of the assembly is contained in contigs ≥119,681 bp |
| N90 | 31,578 bp | 90% of the assembly is contained in contigs ≥31,578 bp |
| Ns | 0 | No ambiguous `N` bases |
| Gaps | 0 | No gaps represented in the assembly |
| Total assembly length | 5,185,224 bp | All contigs together contain \~5.19 Mb of sequence |

Run the larger flye dataset:

`#!/bin/bash #SBATCH --time=360 #SBATCH --ntasks=4 --mem=10gb`

`echo "Starting flye in $(pwd) at $(date)"`

`flye --nano-raw amtp4_20x.fastq --out-dir amtp4_20x --genome-size 5m --threads 4`

`echo "Finished flye in $(pwd) at $(date)"`

... and then run `sbatch run_flye_large.sh` in the terminal.

Use the `assembly-stats` program to assess the contiguity and completeness of this assembly.

```{bash}
assembly-stats amtp4_20x/assembly.fasta
```

**Table 4:** Assembly outputs from the large flye dataset

| STATISTIC | RESULT | MEANING |
|------------------------|-----------------|-------------------------------|
| Total assembly length | 7,453,463 bp | All contigs together contain \~7.45 Mb of sequence |
| Number of contigs | 53 | The assembly is split into 53 separate pieces |
| Average contig length | 140,631 bp | Mean contig size is \~140.6 kb |
| Largest contig | 3,378,256 bp | The longest continuous assembled sequence is \~3.38 Mb |
| N50 | 1,775,265 bp | 50% of the assembly is contained in contigs ≥1,775,265 bp |
| N90 | 44,872 bp | 90% of the assembly is contained in contigs ≥44,872 bp |
| Ns | 0 | No ambiguous `N` bases |
| **Gaps** | **0** | No gaps represented in the assembly |
| Total assembly length | 7,453,463 bp | All contigs together contain \~7.45 Mb of sequence |

The 20× Flye assembly is way more contiguous than the standard Flye assembly.
